title: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

sense.text:
There is a stir going on in Israel over a doctrine of Christianity that says the nations can be saved. It comes from being orphans: no proper guidance, running away from daddy's house, out on your own, and you wander off into the darkness. We have seen it before. In 2018 brothers left this body, and all of a sudden the Sabbath begins at sunrise. Where is the sunrise Sabbath camp now? Nowhere to be found. That is what happens when you stray from the ones you know and bite the hand that feeds you.

Peter names the men who carry it: “But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government.” That is what it boils down to. Having multiple women, concubines — you are in captivity and you are teaching that you can have concubines; you are a concubine yourself. You are in slavery and you teach that you can have slaves, slave wives. You cannot make it up.

“and despise government.” They despise being led. They want to lead when they are not leaders, when they lack the experience and the time to lead. They do not want to be told what to do, they do not want an elder over them, because they feel they are already the elder and already the priest. Those are the attributes of men who seek preeminence they are not worthy of.

“Presumptuous are they, selfwilled.” Presumptuous is saying the elders and the old school taught that the nation is going to be saved, when the men who sat in those rooms are still here and were never taught any such thing. Self-willed is going off on your own and doing whatever you want with no instruction and no guidance, which puts you right back at presumptuous. And “they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities” — not afraid to disrespect the men who were around long before their time: going against their own elders, defecting from them, deserters.

precepts.why:
Jude addressed the same thing in the same words: “Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.” Two readers, one charge. Peter had the time to address this, and so did Jude.

“despise dominion” is despising being led — wanting to be a leader when you are not built to be one, when you lack the time and the experience for it. How do you know? By their actions, by their decorum, by the pride and the arrogance in them. Not been in the world twenty years, running their mouth because they have a YouTube page, against men who were out teaching in the street in Brooklyn when they were seven years old. They do not know who we are.

“and speak evil of dignities” — speaking evil of leadership, of men who were around long before their time, on the strength of some book with dubious dating. They speak on it anyway, and they have never once asked the men who were there.

sense.text:
“But these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed” — the same ones mentioned in verse 10. Some are predestined for death, and their own actions and their own teachings make it so.

“speak evil of the things that they understand not.” Like Paul teaching idolatry. Things in that realm. If Paul was teaching idolatry, that makes Paul a false prophet: the scriptures say Paul was used as a chosen vessel, and Paul says in his letters that he was taught by Christ himself. A man taught by Christ who then writes a letter saying you can worship other gods and be an idolater is a false prophet, and that is the end of it. But rather than be honest and outright about it, brothers want to be discreet and slick: we are not saying he is a false prophet, he just made a mistake. So let us be clear about what is being said — Paul taught us to worship other gods or idols, and he is a righteous man we take instruction from.

A mistake is what Peter did when he denied Christ three times, which Christ had already called, or when he was ashamed to teach the northern kingdom and hid himself off. That is a mistake that can be fixed and rectified. When you tell someone in a letter to serve or reverence another god, that is far from an error and far from a mistake. That is idolatry.

Follow what it would mean. We serve an incompetent God who allowed a man to write letters ten and twenty years before the gospels, full of garbage, while Peter sat there oblivious, and Christ was up there asleep until somebody woke him to say Paul is writing erroneous letters — and his answer was to raise up unlearned men down here with no elders to show the world that Paul was off. That is what we are supposed to believe: that our God is incompetent and the disciples Christ chose were incompetent. And this is not new. It starts with the old man who taught that garbage years ago and spawned these rebellious children. They are his fault. They are his children, and now they are causing all this confusion.

precepts.why:
Peter read Paul's letters, and he says how many: “As also in all his epistles.” All of them. Not some in all his epistles, not a few — all his letters. Paul wrote Corinthians around 54 or 55 AD and Peter was alive and right there, with many surviving disciples around him, Andrew and John among them.

“speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.” Hard to be understood, but see who they are hard for: the unlearned and the unstable. The same men out of chapter 2 — the self-willed, the presumptuous, the uncleanness. Unstable is one minute the nations cannot be saved, now they can; they are all wicked, now some of them are good. And they wrest the other scriptures the same way, the ones about nations going into captivity and not being saved. “unto their own destruction” — the destruction Peter already said they were reserved for.

“beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.” So the ones who wrestle and have a hard time with Paul's letters are the wicked, and that is the error of the wicked; the steadfastness you fall from is Paul's letters. And Peter was the elder of the twelve. If Paul wrote idolatry and Peter read every letter and left it there, then Peter was complicit, and if Peter is wrong the other eleven are wrong, because James was already killed by Herod. What Peter actually says is “But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.”

“But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.” Word for word what Peter said about the same men, by another hand.

“Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain.” Cain hated his brother and despised him, and that spirit is in this doctrine. When you teach that your brother's enemies can be saved along with him, you are Cain. When you teach that the man who raped and massacred our people, and celebrates their death on this very day, can get salvation because there are a few good ones, you despise your own people. And we are the ones called the Christian camp, while they are the ones teaching nation salvation.

“and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward.” Balaam wanted that money — the fancy car, the G Wagon. He did it for reward. “and perished in the gainsaying of Core.” Core's charge against Moses was that you think you are better than us, you look down on us. That is the same charge being made now. The exact same spirit.

sense.text:
“Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” Whom will God teach knowledge, and make to understand how to teach his Bible and how to speak his words? The ones who were nourished — by parents, by elders, by the word of God. The ones who have guidance. A baby cannot teach itself how to drink milk or how to walk.

These are the rules of engagement, and they answer a new trend. Israel is getting real weak with the scriptures now, real passive, and beginning to adapt. Back then the elders did not use a bunch of blue letter Bible, a bunch of different versions, commentaries. They went to Times Square with the KJB and nothing else and set the place on fire. These men were a problem for the world, which is why they had to be destroyed and infiltrated — they knew these men were a problem. Now all of a sudden it is the blue letter and the Greek and eight versions for one verse.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.” It does not say precept must be upon commentary. It does not say precept upon different versions, or precept upon the Strong's, or precept upon the concordance. Precept must be upon precept.

That is not a ban on ever opening one. If it corroborates with the precepts, if it supports the precepts, then it is usable. If it does not, it is garbage. What is being asked here is why eight versions for one verse — the NLT, the ASV, whatever is next. There is something or someone behind this new adaptation of teaching, and it is Satan; there is evil behind it. That was not how it was taught in 2006 under Bishop, with no concordances and no blue letter.

The Bible is self-explanatory; it does not need the help. Greek is in the Bible. Gentile is in the Bible. We explain it from the Bible, and when we use the precepts the Christians cannot deal with us. Of course black folks love white folks, so we will use the white man's commentary to make black folks feel more comfortable — oh, the white man said it, now I understand. That is sarcasm, and it is the point: we do not need the commentary unless it correlates with the precepts the Bible already states. Those precepts were there before there was a concordance and before there was a Strong's.

precepts.why:
“Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” That is saying the exact same thing as “them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” The man God teaches knowledge to is the man who studied and is approved, who has no need to be ashamed of how he handles it.

“rightly dividing the word of truth” is the dividing Isaiah already described: “here a little, and there a little.” Precept upon precept. That is what rightly dividing looks like in practice, and it is why the precepts are enough on their own.

And it comes through Paul, which is the whole point of the morning. Listen to Paul, because Paul was chosen by Christ. Paul was no false prophet. By what Peter says, if you do not understand Paul's letters, you are the wicked. Peter did not say that Paul messes up from time to time, or that sometimes he is off, or never mind Paul.

sense.text:
“And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.” This is the kingdom. The kingdoms of the earth and the lower kingdoms were passed away. They are gone.

“and there was no more sea.” Does that mean there are no more oceans and no more rivers? No. So how do we know what it means? You cannot go to the commentary and find out what sea means — it is not going to tell you. The precepts tell you. This is a precept upon precept class, staying in one version, and this one verse is the example.

The sea is the nations. No more sea is no more nations, gone, made to disappear. That is what John saw, and that is what God is going to do.

precepts.why:
“And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” The waters John saw, where the whore of Babylon sits, are nations. So the sea is the nations, said plainly in the same book John is writing.

See how easy that was. Three chapters over from the verse we are reading, and no Strong's was needed for it, no commentary, no second version. Quick and easy.

That is the first rule being demonstrated: the Bible gave the definition itself, in the same hand and almost in the same breath, which is why the sea in the new heaven and new earth is not water at all.

Now the Old Testament, to see that waters and seas are synonymous. “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.” The waters under the heaven — because there are waters above the heaven too, called space; deep space is water. The water under that is the water on the earth.

“And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas.” The gathering together of the waters, he called seas. So waters and seas are the same thing, named by God himself at the beginning. Be alive and aware of that.

Put it back with what was read as a parable in Revelation: the waters are peoples and nations, and the waters are the seas. Seas, waters, nations — one and the same, from the first chapter of the Bible to the last book of it.

David asks to be delivered out of the waters, and in the same breath he says who the waters are: “Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children.” The great waters are strange children. Other nations. He says it twice, because he closes with “Rid me, and deliver me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.”

And right in the middle of it is who gets salvation: “It is he that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword.” Not salvation unto all nations. Unto kings. The kings are us. “I will sing a new song unto thee, O God” — that is in the kingdom.

So nations are referred to as great waters, and great waters are called seas; today we call them oceans. When John says there was no more sea, the thing that is gone is the hand of strange children that David asked to be delivered from.

This is when Christ returns. “God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran.” Teman is Edom. He comes out from among them. And keep the Holy One in mind — that is important to remember.

“His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.” Then: “And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power.” Power beams in his hand. And the hiding of his power is him holding it back, because he could destroy everything if he wanted to.

That is who is coming before the question about the rivers and the sea is ever asked. The one with the hidden power in his hand is the one who empties the sea in Revelation.

“Was the Lord displeased against the rivers? was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?” Does that mean Christ comes back angry at the Harlem River? Mad at the ocean? No. It is the nations here. Rivers, great waters, sea — the same thing, the same people, in a prophet who never names them any other way.

“thy chariots of salvation.” Chariots of salvation. Hold that word; who those chariots are for gets settled before this is over.

“Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word.” According to the oaths of the tribes. The bow comes out over an oath sworn to the tribes, not to the rivers and not to the sea.

“Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.” In indignation, and he threshes the heathen in anger. Not some of the heathen. Not the heathen except the good ones. The heathen.

“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed.” For the salvation of thy people — not thy people and other people that are good. And are all nations anointed? No. The salvation that goes forth goes forth with the anointed.

“thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked, by discovering the foundation unto the neck.” He cut the head off. He conquered the main nation, the top nation, and the head is Edom.

“Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” The multitude of many people makes a noise like the seas, and the nations rush like mighty waters. The two words are laid side by side in one verse.

David said deliver me from great waters. Here: “The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but God shall rebuke them.” That is the rebuke we just read in Habakkuk 3, where his wrath was against the sea.

“and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.” Chased off like chaff and like a rolling thing. That is what no more sea looks like when it happens.

“And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.” The nations hide. The bombers they call bunker busters, the last-day preppers — the elites and the ones with the money, and the Arabs and the Asians too, who have the underground and mountainous places to hide in when Christ returns.

“when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth” is nuclear destruction. And then: “In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats.” The gods they built get thrown to the moles and the bats on the way into the hole. “To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks.”

And if they are going to be saved, why are they hiding? Why would you be hiding if the Lord is coming to save you and give you salvation? Why build the bunkers? They will say the bunkers are for the elites. Whatever.

So while the nations run and hide from the destruction, what are we doing? “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.” The land of the north is the head of the wicked, the capital.

“and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” From all the lands, because Israel is scattered all over the world and not just in America. Israel is international.

“Behold, I will send for many fishers, saith the Lord, and they shall fish them.” That is what we are doing right now: we travel, we go out there and we fish for our people who are scattered among these waters. He says fish because they are scattered among the waters, and the waters are nations. Then, after Israel is fished up and gathered: “and after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks” — the same holes Isaiah put them in. We hunt them down like animals. Nowhere in it do they get saved along with us; they are hiding, and being spared from destruction is not salvation. There is no chariot marked for a good Edomite, no chariot marked for a good Moabite. There are no good heathen chariots. None.

“For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” Israel is God's elect. Read it again and let it sit: Jacob my servant, and Israel mine elect.

Now the demand, and it is a fair one. One precept of scripture that shows any nation outside of the Israelites that is good and is called God's elect. One. Where does God say that Edomite right there, he is the elect, he is good? Yes, sir, master is good, master gave me a G Wagon — there is no such verse.

Maybe Christ is lying, the same way they say he made Paul lie. Or the verse says what it says and nobody else is in it.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” Because of the shaking, because of nuclear destruction, they hide in the mountains. That is what the holes of the rocks are for.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads.” Look up. The chariots are going to show up, and those are the chariots of salvation Habakkuk already rode in on.

“for your redemption draweth nigh.” Your redemption. Not everyone's redemption. Not all the good nations' redemption. Your redemption draweth nigh.

The exact same account, for anybody who will not take Luke because he was not one of the twelve. “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.” That tribulation is Jacob's trouble. It does not say Jacob and the heathen's trouble. Why would the Lord save the nations out of no trouble? What trouble is theirs? This is their world.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” His elect. Not his elect and then some. Not his elect and some good nations. His elect, gathered from the four winds of heaven. Show one good Edomite in the Bible who is called an elect. Give one heathen that God calls his elect because he was good to Israel. One nation. One.

There is no scripture where the elect are the nations that are good. This is house doctrine for trying to save mama and grandma, and you are not saving grandma and mama. It does not matter how good her bland chicken tastes or how good her raisined potato salad tastes. You are not saving them.
